subject: Integration hypotheses & prioritized risks for Embedding + Rerank pilot
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novamed.com>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Integration hypotheses & prioritized risks for Embedding + Rerank pilot

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the time. This thread captures what we heard, the hypotheses we want to validate in the pilot, and the immediate asks so we can scope a short POC (3–4 weeks). Please correct anything I mis-stated.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Search results are inconsistent between product and clinical QA; manual reranking is common and costly.
- Latency spikes in bulk batch scoring (they process nightly batches of updated patient summaries).
- Need structured outputs for downstream EHR ingestion (JSON schema required).

Pilot goals (mutually agreed):
1) Surface a reranking layer that improves clinical relevance by +15% on your internal metric (click-through to validated notes).
2) Keep 99th-percentile latency under 500ms for single-query rerank, and sub-5s for 1000-item batch jobs.
3) Deliver a structured output schema for the top-3 suggestions that maps to your EHR import fields.

Technical hypotheses (to validate in POC):
- H1: Embedding similarity + a lightweight reranker (Cross-encoder 2-stage) will reduce manual review by >20% on triage queries.
- H2: Using Redwood streaming + function-calling to emit structured JSON reduces parsing mismatches vs. free text.
- H3: Prefix KV caching for batch scoring reduces per-item GPU cost by ~30% for nightly jobs.

Constraints you flagged:
- On-prem data policy: PHI cannot be sent to public endpoints. You will evaluate Redwood Private in a later phase; for the POC we will run without PHI (de-identified subset).
- Token budgets: cost sensitivity at scale; need clear unit economics before expanding beyond pilot.
- Schema strictness: the EHR pipeline requires an exact field set; any change requires sign-off from your integration team.

Proposed POC scope (week-by-week):
- Week 1: Sample dataset ingestion (de-id), agree acceptance criteria, wire sample prompt set and structured schema.
- Week 2: Prototype embedding index + candidate retrieval; compare similarity baselines.
- Week 3: Integrate reranker (streaming + funcalls) and produce structured outputs; run batch job.
- Week 4: Evaluation against acceptance criteria, QA pass, and pilot retrospective.

Immediate asks from Redwood: 
- Delivery: a de-identified sample of 2k queries + expected structured schema mapping (attachment: sample_prompt_set.json).
- Technical contacts: confirm the integration owner who will accept the SFTP/drive ingest and approve schema.
- Contract: sign a short SOW — attaching a stub (redwood_sow_stub.pdf) for terms, timeline, and price band for pilot.

Attachments: integration_hypotheses_matrix.xlsx (hypotheses / metrics), sample_prompt_set.json, redwood_sow_stub.pdf

Next steps / owners:
- Lena: provide the de-id dataset and schema by Tue 2027-05-25.
- Ben: I (Chloe) will act as primary technical PM for Redwood. Ben will own pricing and SOW.
- Marcus: own model selection and perf validation in the POC.

If that all sounds right we'll lock dates and issue the SOW. Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novamed.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@novamed.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration hypotheses & prioritized risks for Embedding + Rerank pilot

Thanks Chloe — this is a great summary and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side:
- Dataset: we'll deliver a de-id pull of ~2.5k queries plus the associated clinician annotations. Expect delivery by COB Tue (2027-05-25).
- Schema: Carlos will share the EHR field mapping (he's on this thread).
- PHI guardrails: for the POC we agree de-id only; we will evaluate Private deployment options in parallel for later stages.

Priority-wise we want: 1) structured outputs that map cleanly into EHR, 2) low-latency single-query rerank, 3) batch cost improvements. Happy for Redwood to prioritize the pilot in that order.

Also, can you confirm the minimal SDK/API changes you'd expect on our side for function calling and streaming? We have a small integration team and want to surface the dev effort.

Lena
VP Product, NovaMed
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novamed.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration hypotheses & prioritized risks for Embedding + Rerank pilot

Lena — quick answers on dev effort and commercial next steps:
- SDK/API impact: For function-calling + streaming we expect 2–3 small integration points:
  1) Call the Redwood SDK stream endpoint for reranker inference (single POST with streaming JSON chunks) — we provide JS/Python examples that are ~15–30 lines.
  2) Implement a short adapter that consumes streamed funcall outputs into your existing ingestion pipeline (we can provide a reference adapter for Node/Python).
  3) Batch jobs: a one-off job to invoke the batch scoring API; no persistent integration required beyond scheduling.
Estimated dev effort: 2 dev-days to wire an initial streaming funcall integration; additional 1–2 days to validate schema mapping and error handling.

Commercial / SOW notes:
- I'll share the pilot SOW with the banded pricing — goal is to keep the pilot cost predictable. Attachment: redwood_sow_stub.pdf.
- If NovaMed wants an on-prem/private option after the pilot we can fast-track an architecture review (separate engagement).

I'll draft a short SOW and ping for signatures once we have the dataset and schema.

Ben
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
